title: Bridgeway - Embeddings & Hosting Options Discovery
meeting_header: 2026-11-02 16:00 UTC | 46 minutes | Bridgeway Analytics x Redwood Inference | Attendees: Alex Chen (AE), Priya Nair (SE) - Redwood; Markus Vogel (CTO), Aisha Khan (Head of Search), Devon Lee (Infra) - Bridgeway.
summary: Discovery focused on embeddings/rerank architecture, vector DB integration choices, throughput projections, and hosting tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC). Customer emphasized strict PII controls, SOC2 + regional residency, and a Q4 pilot target. SE offered a benchmark plan and suggested quantized embeddings + hybrid rerank for cost/latency balance.
transcript:
00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we've got about 45 minutes. Quick intro, I'm Alex from Redwood, joined by Priya our solution engineer. 00:22 Markus Vogel: Yeah hi, Markus here, CTO at Bridgeway Analytics. We all good. 00:28 Aisha Khan: Aisha - Head of Search. We want to talk embed pipeline and where to run it. 00:35 Alex Chen: Cool. Could you start with current infra and volumes? 00:42 Devon Lee: Sure, we run a mixed infra. Primary search is Elastic for metadata, we use a self-hosted vector DB (open source) for embeddings right now; throughput spikes are common, like 2k-3k embedding requests per minute during biz hours, and rerank calls are bursty on search pages. 01:05 Priya Nair: Ok do you do embeddings online sync or batch? 01:09 Devon Lee: Hybrid - initial batch for backlog and then online upsert for user content. 01:15 Aisha Khan: Our latency SLO for search front-end is 300ms P95, and rerank can be slightly higher but we prefer sub-200ms for the second stage. 01:27 Alex Chen: Makes sense. When you say self-hosted vector DB, are you on Milvus/Pinecone-managed or custom? 01:35 Devon Lee: It's a custom fork of Milvus, running on k8s. We found some ops pain with sharding and rebalances. 01:41 Markus Vogel: The key drivers for us are: cost predictability, strict data controls (no raw vectors leaving our VPC for PII content), and reproducible quality — we measure NDCG for rerank. 01:56 Priya Nair: Understood. We usually evaluate three hosting options: Redwood Hosted API (fast to start), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), or Redwood Private which runs in your VPC / on-prem. Sounds like Private might be interesting because of the PII requirement. 02:15 Aisha Khan: Yes, private is attractive. But we also want to know performance delta — is Dedicated near-hosted in latency? 02:24 Alex Chen: In many cases dedicated is near-hosted; the difference comes down to networking and scale. Hosted has global infra, and Dedicated gives you reserved capacity co-located with predictable throughput. Private adds your network egress and KMS controls so slightly more tail latency depending on connectivity. 02:44 Devon Lee: What about KV cache and prefix caching? We rely on KV for session state but would like auto cache for repeated prefixes. 02:52 Priya Nair: Our runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching. For heavy rerank workloads we often recommend KV cache + short TTLs to keep tail latency low. 03:04 Markus Vogel: On embeddings: we're using 1536-d vectors today. We're debating lowering dims to 768 to save cost, but worried about recall drop. 03:16 Priya Nair: Tradeoffs there are workload dependent. For semantic retrieval 1536 can help, but quantization (int8/4) plus a smaller dimension can often preserve NDCG if you tune the reranker. We suggested running a dimension sweep in eval. 03:33 Aisha Khan: Would Redwood run that eval or do we run locally? 03:38 Alex Chen: We can run a joint eval — our Optimize toolkit will suggest quantization and dim profiles given a sample corpus and query set. We usually do a small A/B on reranker quality. 03:50 Devon Lee: Integration with our vector DB: we want to avoid wholesale migration. Can Redwood handle hybrid search where topk from our DB is combined with Redwood embeddings/rerank? 03:59 Priya Nair: Yes, hybrid setups are common — you can do vector fanout from your DB to Redwood's rerank model or call Redwood to generate embeddings and push to your DB; we support both. Also fallback routing to a cheaper quantized model for lower SLAs. 04:18 Markus Vogel: Any constraints on throughput per second? Our spike profile is 200 qps for rerank at peak. 04:25 Priya Nair: For rerank at 200 qps we'd look at Dedicated or Private with reserved GPUs. Hosted can handle it but cost unpredictability during sustained spikes is a concern. We recommend a dedicated pool with autoscale and burst capacity. 04:39 Aisha Khan: How do you shard embedding compute if our DB is sharded? 04:45 Priya Nair: We align shard topology with your DB fanout; Redwood's routing can route requests by shard key to the right serving pool, which reduces cross-shard copies and KV cache misses. 04:58 Devon Lee: Security questions: do you provide SOC2 docs, SSO, SAML, and KMS integration? 05:06 Alex Chen: Yes to all. We provide SOC2 Type II reports, SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning; in Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management. 05:18 Markus Vogel: For Private, is the control plane still Redwood-hosted? 05:22 Alex Chen: Usually yes — control plane can be in Redwood but with strict audit logs and RBAC; we also offer fully air-gapped options for certain regs but that is a contract-level discussion. 05:33 Aisha Khan: About benchmarks — can we run an on-prem perf test for our real queries? 05:37 Priya Nair: Absolutely. We usually run a smoke benchmark with your sample traffic, evaluating P50/P95/P99 and token cost. We'll need a small dataset and a few thousand queries to be representative. 05:50 Devon Lee: On cost, what levers do we have? 05:53 Priya Nair: Model size, quantization level, batching config, and routing policies. For embeddings cost we can push quantized float8/int4 and reduce dims; for rerank model we can use a smaller distilled model for the first-pass and full model for final ranking. 06:09 Markus Vogel: Our timeline is Q4 pilot, production in Q1. We need security review next week if possible. 06:16 Alex Chen: Noted. We'll send security pack and a pilot scope doc. 06:20 Aisha Khan: Actionable: we'd like a clear plan: integration steps with our vector DB, benchmark run, and pilot pricing. 06:27 Priya Nair: We'll propose a 4-week pilot: week 1 bootstrap + connectivity, week 2 perf/quality eval, week 3 config tuning (quant/dim), week 4 run pilot traffic and final report. 06:40 Devon Lee: For connectivity, our infra sits in AWS eu-west-2 and we use private VPC peering for critical data. Can Redwood support VPC peering? 06:49 Alex Chen: Yes for Private and Dedicated we can peer; Hosted supports TLS+private IP via partner connections in some regions. 06:58 Aisha Khan: Any gotchas on vector serialization/compatibility? 07:02 Priya Nair: We support common vector formats (float32 arrays, int8 packs) and have small adapters for Milvus/FAISS/Weaviate. Expect small conversions but nothing major. 07:14 Markus Vogel: Competitors we looked at: Pinecone, built-in vendor endpoints and some self-hosted toolchains. 07:21 Alex Chen: Right. Our differentiation: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, cost controls and routing policy, and first-class eval tooling. 07:30 Aisha Khan: Questions about SLA: what's your typical P95 uptime for Dedicated? 07:34 Alex Chen: We offer SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated (99.9+) and monitoring hooks; full SLA in contract. 07:41 Devon Lee: Can you demonstrate end-to-end latency numbers for a sample rerank flow? 07:44 Priya Nair: We'll share a benchmark sheet; rough numbers now: optimized rerank on 1-2 GPUs gives sub-100ms P95 for short context and cached KV; without caching expect higher. 07:59 Markus Vogel: Good. Next steps? 08:02 Alex Chen: We'll send security docs, pilot scope, pricing matrix, and a short list of data needed. Also schedule SE-led benchmark next Tue if that works. 08:14 Aisha Khan: Tue works. We'll prepare an eval set, 5k queries and sample docs, and an infra contact for peering. 08:22 Devon Lee: I'll be the infra contact, email devon@bridgeway.ai. 08:26 Alex Chen: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and links. 08:31 End of recording.

Note: transcript contains occasional ASR mis-hearings and truncated words, e.g., 'Redwood dedicate' instead of 'Redwood Dedicated', 'KV cash' for 'KV cache'.
